curriculum.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
curriculum.description: Students analyze a read-aloud passage to extract the main idea or central message through systematic text evidence collection. Focus: Determining the overall point or central message of the narrative or text. Examples: The importance of kindness, the lesson learned by the protagonist, the significance of the invention, the moral of the fable, the primary topic of the report, why the animal adapted to its habitat, how weather affects the local ecosystem, the reason for the city festival. Constraints: The passage-studio must provide a short text segment where the student chooses the one best sentence that summarizes the entire passage from a list of distractors.

status: authored; catalog-checked; each binding generator-probed once; not hydrated as a lesson; not runtime-tested
learnerAction: Listen to a read-aloud story and choose the one sentence that sums up the whole story, not a single detail.

components.title: Why Did It Happen?
components.intent: Grade 2 read-aloud stories where a character makes a choice; the child says why.

components.title: Read and Listen: The Garden
components.intent: Grade 2 story of 80-120 words with one clear central message; tutor reads it aloud. Include one question asking which sentence best tells what the whole story is about, with detail-only distractors.

evidenceCriteria: Chooses the whole-story summary over true-but-narrow details. No listening primitive asks this today: passage-studio is text-first and its recall mode has no main-idea item; decodable-reader main_idea needs the child to read.
coverageLimits: media-player story_analysis is not usable as drawn: segment 4 narrates the answer, and the script stays printed during questions at grade 1+.
story-talk stories are 3-5 sentences and its answers are single words, so it cannot carry a summary sentence choice.
